title: Generic prime-constant filtration step in second cohomology
statement: Let k be algebraically closed and D/k a smooth integral affine connected curve [def-sc-curves], with generic inclusion eta:Spec k(D) to D [def-sc-function-field]. Let S be a short exact sequence of generic abelian etale sheaves, with third term isomorphic to the constant Z/ell sheaf [def-sc-constant-sheaves] for a prime ell. If H²(D,Z/ell) and H²(D,eta_*S.X_1) are subsingleton [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], then H²(D,eta_*S.X_2) is subsingleton. No finiteness hypothesis on the first or second term is needed.

proof.text: Apply generic direct image to S. Finite-limit preservation gives exactness and monicity on the left. Let beta be the pushed-forward last map, I its abelian image and Q its cokernel. Factor beta through I. The exactness comparison with the monic image inclusion produces a short exact sequence G1 to G2 to I. The kernel-cokernel sequence I to G3 to Q is short exact.

The generic counit is invertible. Naturality identifies generic inverse image of beta with S.g up to invertible maps; hence it is epic. Inverse image preserves cokernels as a left adjoint, so generic inverse image of Q is zero. Therefore its generic adjunction unit is zero. On every affine etale object, continuity at the function-field limit shrinks a nonempty affine open until the image of any section under its open unit is zero. Affine etale objects form a covering basis, so Q has generically vanishing sections. Generic acyclicity gives H1(Q)=0.

Smoothness gives integrally closed local rings and thus normality of D; finite type gives Noetherianity. Apply normal generic constant comparison for the finite group ULift ZMod ell. The residue map at the generic point is invertible because its stalk is the function field. Composition coherence of adjunction units cancels this residue-field isomorphism and gives the constant comparison for fromSpecFunctionField. Transport along e and use hconstant to obtain H2(G3)=0.

Use the existing Ext long exact sequence, which computes Sheaf.H directly. Exactness at H2(I) in I to G3 to Q and H1(Q)=0 implies H2(I)=0. Exactness at H2(G2) in G1 to G2 to I and hfirst then implies H2(G2)=0. The Lean proof explicitly chooses the preimages and shows they are zero.
